design.root_cause: FancyZones rebuilds every `WorkArea` whenever the virtual desktop ID changes, even if the monitor set and geometry are unchanged. Desktop switches therefore tear down and recreate every `ZonesOverlay` window, matching the reporter's PresentMon evidence and the `ShouldWorkAreasBeRecreated` check on `UniqueId().virtualDesktopId`.
evidence: Issue #27555 is labeled `Priority-1` and the latest report on 0.100.2 includes A/B PresentMon measurements showing DWM freezes are materially worse with FancyZones enabled.

The latest issue comment points directly at `FancyZones::ShouldWorkAreasBeRecreated()` and notes that `UniqueId().virtualDesktopId != virtualDesktop` is true on every virtual desktop switch, forcing `UpdateWorkAreas()` to clear and rebuild all work areas.

In `src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/FancyZones.cpp`, `UpdateWorkAreas` calls `m_workAreaConfiguration.Clear()` whenever `ShouldWorkAreasBeRecreated` returns true, which destroys each `WorkArea`, its `ZonesOverlay`, and the pooled overlay HWND bookkeeping.

In `src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/WorkArea.h`, the work-area identity is stored as `const FancyZonesDataTypes::WorkAreaId m_uniqueId`, so the current implementation cannot simply retag existing work areas for the new desktop.

affected_files.purpose: Decides when work areas are rebuilt and currently clears them on every virtual-desktop change.
Defines the work-area identity and needs a way to refresh the virtual-desktop portion without destroying the overlay window.
Owns layout/history initialization that must be refreshed in place after a desktop switch.
Existing WorkArea tests can cover in-place virtual-desktop retagging and layout refresh.
Verifies per-desktop layout bookkeeping so a desktop switch keeps the right layout without forcing a full rebuild.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: A virtual-desktop ID mismatch is treated the same as monitor removal or geometry change, so `UpdateWorkAreas()` always clears and rebuilds every work area on desktop switch.
implementation_steps.change: Split the decision into `NoChange`, `DesktopContextChanged`, and `Recreate`, so desktop-only changes refresh existing work areas in place instead of clearing them.
edge_cases: True monitor add/remove and work-area-rect changes must still force full recreation.
The span-zones-across-monitors path needs the same decision split as the per-monitor path.
tests: Add a test/helper assertion that a desktop-ID-only change does not hit the destructive clear/recreate branch.
Manual: switch virtual desktops repeatedly and confirm overlays are no longer recreated every time in logs.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Each `WorkArea` stores a const `m_uniqueId`, so the only way to move to a new desktop identity today is to destroy the object and create a new one.
implementation_steps.change: Allow the virtual-desktop component of the work-area ID to be updated in place and expose a focused refresh method that rebinds layout/history for the new desktop without destroying the overlay HWND.
edge_cases: Monitor identity and work-area rect must remain immutable for the lifetime of the existing HWND.
The refresh method must preserve the pooled overlay window and current renderer unless geometry really changed.
tests: Unit-test that `RefreshForVirtualDesktop` updates `UniqueId()` and keeps the work-area window alive.
Unit-test that per-desktop layout lookup follows the refreshed desktop ID.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Layout and snapped-window initialization happen only when a new `WorkArea` is created, so desktop switches currently piggyback on destructive rebuilds.
implementation_steps.change: Implement an in-place refresh that updates `m_uniqueId.virtualDesktopId`, clones or applies the layout for the new desktop when needed, recalculates the zone set, and reinitializes snapped windows without freeing the overlay window.
edge_cases: Do not duplicate zone-history entries when windows are re-snapped under the new desktop ID.
Avoid flashing overlays during a passive desktop switch unless the user is actively dragging.
tests: WorkArea tests should verify that desktop refresh preserves layout geometry and still maps saved zones.
Applied-layout tests should verify the new desktop picks up the previous desktop layout without a full rebuild.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: There is no regression test guarding the desktop-switch path that currently rebuilds overlays.
implementation_steps.change: Add focused tests for in-place desktop refresh and for preserving layout/history after the virtual-desktop ID changes.
edge_cases: Tests must use fixed GUIDs and deterministic layouts.
If the unit-test environment cannot instantiate a real overlay, assert through the identity and layout IDs instead.
tests: Run the FancyZones unit tests covering `WorkArea` and `AppliedLayouts` after adding the desktop-refresh cases.

verify: Run the FancyZones unit tests that cover `WorkArea` and `AppliedLayouts`.
Manual: switch desktops repeatedly with FancyZones enabled and confirm the logs no longer show `Add new work area on virtual desktop` / overlay-pool churn on every switch.
Manual: repeat the reporter's PresentMon A/B capture and confirm desktop-switch freezes materially drop when FancyZones remains enabled.
risks: Per-desktop layouts and app-zone history are keyed by `WorkAreaId`, so mutating the desktop ID in place must not corrupt saved layout lookups.
If refresh-in-place misses a geometry-changing case, overlays can become stale until the next full rebuild.
alternatives: Keep recreating work areas and only debounce the rebuild path. Rejected because the evidence shows the rebuild itself is the dominant cost.
Disable or bypass the overlay window pool. Rejected because it hides one symptom while leaving the unnecessary full rebuild in place.
